population.definition: Maputo Cidade (the city, which is also a province-level unit), census count of 1 August 2017, not adjusted for underenumeration. Maputo Provincia (the separate surrounding province) was 1,908,078 in the same census per the same source. Note: Urban Resilience Hub quotes 1,273,076 for the city citing INE 2017, which conflicts and is not used.

source.title: Maputo Cidade
source.publisher: citypopulation.de (compiles Instituto Nacional de Estatistica Mocambique)
source.quote: The tabulated population figures are not adjusted for underenumeration.

places.name: Maputo Central Railway Station
places.what: A railway terminus in the city centre, built in the colonial period with a copper-clad dome. Its design is credited to Alfredo Augusto Lisboa de Lima and Mario Veiga, with the dome by José Ferreira da Costa.

source.title: Maputo — Lourenço Marques and African Art Déco
source.author: Luigi De Marchi
source.quote: The railway station anchors any first impression.

source.title: Maputo — Lourenço Marques and African Art Déco
source.author: Luigi De Marchi
source.quote: a Beaux-Arts statement of the colony's ambitions

facts.label: Eiffel attribution (conflict)
facts.value: EBSCO attributes the station to Eiffel and dates it to 1910, which conflicts with the architect names above. Treat the Eiffel link as disputed; do not state it as fact.

source.title: Maputo, Mozambique
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: Eiffel also designed Maputo's railway station, which dates to 1910.

places.name: Fortaleza de Maputo (Maputo Fortress)
places.what: A Portuguese fortress from the 1780s that now houses the Museum of Military History. The current building dates to the 1940s and the site was classified as a Mozambican Cultural Heritage Monument in 2002.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Built by the Portuguese in the 1780s on earlier Dutch and Austrian fortifications.

source.title: Writing with bodies: installing a new history of Mozambique from Maputo Fortress
source.author: Roberto Conduru
source.quote: was built by Portuguese in 1780s on the ruins of previous fortifications built by Dutch and Austrians.

facts.label: Attack and rebuilding
facts.value: Burned by French corsairs at the end of the 18th century and rebuilt by the Portuguese several times.

source.title: Writing with bodies: installing a new history of Mozambique from Maputo Fortress
source.author: Roberto Conduru
source.quote: French corsairs conquered and burned it down at the end of 18th century.

source.title: Writing with bodies: installing a new history of Mozambique from Maputo Fortress
source.author: Roberto Conduru
source.quote: Deprived of its original functions, the old fortress is now the Museum of Military History.

facts.label: Heritage status
facts.value: Classified in 2002 as a Mozambican Cultural Heritage Monument; current building dates to the 1940s.

source.title: Writing with bodies: installing a new history of Mozambique from Maputo Fortress
source.author: Roberto Conduru
source.quote: the classification it received in 2002 as a Mozambican Cultural Heritage Monument.

places.name: Mercado Central (Central Market)
places.what: The historic municipal market hall in the Baixa, the city centre. A 2011 university dissertation describes it as the only infrastructure provided to support the city's small traders.

facts.label: Role in the city
facts.value: A 2011 architecture dissertation (University of Pretoria) says it was the only infrastructure provided for the city's micro-traders, and that informal street markets had spread north of it.

source.title: Finding the Maputo Central Market: Seeing the Informal Economy in Formal Architecture
source.publisher: University of Pretoria (Master of Architecture dissertation)
source.author: Byron Snow
source.quote: is the only infrastructure provided in support of the micro-enterprisers and traders of the city.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Baixa district; corner of Avenida 25 de Setembro and Rua do Mesquita (as given in dissertation).

source.title: Finding the Maputo Central Market: Seeing the Informal Economy in Formal Architecture
source.author: Byron Snow
source.quote: The low-lying Baixa area of Maputo, is the historic and current city centre of Maputo.

facts.label: Vendors in 2026
facts.value: Fish vendors barred from Praça 25 de Junho say the market has no space or fish storage for them.

source.title: Informal vendors protest ban at Praça 25 de Junho, Maputo
source.quote: At the market, there is no space for us.

places.name: Museu de História Natural (Natural History Museum)
places.what: A natural history museum run by Eduardo Mondlane University, in a Manueline-style building. Its best-known exhibit is a collection of elephant foetuses.

facts.label: Building
facts.value: Housed in a Manueline-style building since 1933.

source.title: Natural History Museum
source.quote: enshrined in a magnificent Manueline architecture style building since 1933

facts.label: Founding
facts.value: UEM page says established in 1911 (another UEM page, not readable, reportedly says 1913; unresolved).

source.title: Natural History Museum
source.quote: The Natural History Museum was established in 1911

facts.label: Collection
facts.value: Elephant foetuses from one to 22 months of development.

source.title: Natural History Museum
source.quote: a collection, probably unique in the world, of elephant fetuses ranging from one month to 22 months old.

source.title: Natural History Museum
source.quote: features a garden with murals painted by Malangatana
